title: Spain holds final televised debate ahead of general election
seoTitle: Spain election: final televised debate held before Sunday vote
dek: Spain is preparing for a general election on 29 November following a parliamentary deadlock and a televised debate among the four main party leaders.
happened: According to reports, Spain is holding a general election on 29 November after Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap vote following a parliamentary deadlock over housing decrees. On 26 November, the four main candidates—Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez of the Socialist Party, Alberto Nunez Feijoo of the conservative People's Party, Santiago Abascal of Vox, and Ada Colau of the left-wing Frente Amplio alliance—participated in a final televised debate in Madrid. The event, moderated by Maria Casado and organized by the Academia de Television, featured discussions on housing, taxation, social policy, corruption, and migration. During the debate, candidates exchanged sharp criticisms over economic policies, housing shortages, corruption investigations, and past handling of regional emergencies. Opposition figures and coalition partners challenged the incumbent administration's record, while the conservative People's Party and Vox maintained a coordinated stance against the prime minister. Voters will head to the polls to elect the 350-seat Congress of Deputies.

sides.says: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez defended his record of economic growth, job creation, and minimum wage increases, while acknowledging past mistakes in housing and trust. During the debate, Sanchez stated, "We have not yet managed to solve the housing problem," and added, "My government has not been perfect. I have made mistakes, I have trusted people I should not have."

Alberto Nunez Feijoo campaigned on a platform of change, criticizing the government over economic management, housing failures, and corruption scandals. Feijoo remarked during the debate regarding housing, "With you, to own a home you have to inherit it, squat in it, or end up in court," and vowed to build one million homes.

Ada Colau criticized both the prime minister and the conservative opposition, arguing that the progressive government had failed to address the housing crisis effectively. Colau told the prime minister, "Mr. Sánchez, I believe much more is expected of the left, and in that sense, I think we must be much more demanding of the progressive government."
Santiago Abascal criticized the incumbent government's policies, immigration stance, and leadership, while presenting his party's manifesto to address the concerns of forgotten citizens.

next: Spaniards will vote in the general election on Sunday, 29 November, to determine the composition of the 350-seat Congress of Deputies.
summary: Spain is holding a general election on 29 November after Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called an early vote due to a parliamentary deadlock on housing measures. The electoral campaign has focused heavily on housing costs, the economy, immigration, and recent corruption controversies. Four main candidates—representing the Socialist Party, the People's Party, Vox, and Frente Amplio—participated in a final televised debate in Madrid on 26 November, clashing over government performance and policy proposals.
